# Geunhyeong Lee, Ph.D.

> Scientist at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), Michigan State University. Engineering devices cannot keep growing as power and energy demands rise, so more performance must come from better design. Geunhyeong Lee's goal is an AI design method, starting from BiSTO, that needs only standard simulations and still works when the physics changes, so that engineers can design, print, and test their own devices and monitor them in operation with digital twins. A physics solver checks each design the AI proposes, and hardware tests check the solver. Background: thermal, fluid, structural, electromagnetic, and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) systems. Generalizing BiSTO to 3D is in progress; digital twins are planned.

This discovery index links to public research, teaching, project, and publication records for Geunhyeong Lee (ORCID: 0000-0003-3141-4663). For the complete plain text academic dossier including full abstracts and career records, see [llms-full.txt](https://geunhyeong.com/llms-full.txt).

## Research philosophy & framework
- Broad vision: Engineering hardware must deliver more performance within a fixed space. Rather than writing separate rules by hand for each device, this research aims at one AI design method, starting from BiSTO, that needs no adjoints and still works when the physics changes.
- Validation philosophy: Trust an AI model only as far as it is checked. A physics solver checks each design proposed by AI, and hardware tests check the solver.
- Framework direction: BiSTO is the core engine: an AI model ranks changes to a layout, and a physics solver checks the best ones, so the method needs only standard simulations. Generalizing it to 3D is in progress. Planned steps: test printed designs in a benchtop loop, apply the same method to electromagnetic pumps and liquid metal MHD, and then use test data to correct the models and build digital twins that detect abnormal behavior.
- Research plan (figure on the Research page): a cycle linking BiSTO design, metal printing, loop tests, and digital twins. Core engine: BiSTO, where an AI model ranks changes and a physics solver checks them. Planned thrusts: thermal, fluid, and structural design in 3D (printable compact heat exchangers and cooling channels); electromagnetic pumps and liquid metal MHD (the same method on new physics); digital twins and anomaly detection (test data corrects the models and the design search). The images in the figure show earlier work; 3D BiSTO, BiSTO hardware tests, and digital twins are planned.

## Research areas & verified highlights
- BiSTO (Binary Surrogate-based Topology Optimization): Neural network surrogate ranks binary solid and fluid updates while connected candidate layouts are verified directly by a turbulent heat transfer solver without flow or turbulence adjoints. Manuscript under review at Applied Thermal Engineering; presented at AM2F 2026 (MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center).
- FRIB Rotating Beam Dump (2024 to Present): Leading the overall fabrication and installation effort across materials, systems engineering, thermomechanics, and radiation for the upgrade beyond 50 kW, targeting 100 kW primary beam power and implementation by 2028 (planned with a BiSTO cooling layout).
- FRIB Static Beam Dump AI Optimization (Nuclear Science and Techniques, 2026): Hybrid genetic algorithm and reinforcement learning approach increasing simulated average power handling capability by 72% over the baseline design.
- AI Designed Nuclear Heat Exchangers (International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer, 2024; Case Studies in Thermal Engineering, 2023): DRL assisted topology optimization achieving 14.8% higher simulated heat transfer than conventional topology optimization, fabricated via metal 3D printing (SUS316L) and tested in a thermal loop.
- 3D Printable DC Electromagnetic Pump (Nuclear Engineering and Technology, 2026; solo author): Single body additive manufacturing concept requiring 52% less simulated input current than a helical pump at matched pressure (10.5 bar) and flow rate.
- Liquid Lithium Charge Stripper & MHD Circulator (Nuclear Engineering and Design, 2023): Reduced MHD circulator weight by 94% (340 kg to 21 kg) and experimentally formed a 22 micrometer liquid lithium film at 200 C.
- Deep Learning Anomaly Detection for KOMAC Linac (Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology, 2025): LSTM autoencoder detecting early fault signatures 30.7 to 286.6 minutes before recorded voltage faults in retrospective operating data.

## Teaching, mentoring & service summary
- Mentoring at FRIB, Michigan State University: Primary or research mentor for 3 students (2 undergraduates, 1 graduate student) on induction heating validation and AI geometry optimization.
- Teaching experience: Lecturer, Foundation of AI (International School on Beam Dynamics and Accelerator Technology, 2023); Instructor, Nuclear Comprehensive Design Project (UNIST, 2016); Teaching Assistant in Electromagnetics, Liquid Metal MHD, and Nuclear Engineering (UNIST, 2017 to 2021); MSU Academy for Teaching participant.
- Credentials & service: Ph.D. in Nuclear Engineering and B.S. in Nuclear Engineering & Mechanical Engineering (UNIST); 35 conference presentations; 6 invited talks; 6 registered Korean patents; 1 registered software program; 32 journal peer reviews across Energy, International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer, Annals of Nuclear Energy, Electronic Research Archive, and related journals.

## Projects


- [Liquid lithium charge stripper](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/em_02_raon_charge_stripper/) (UNIST, 2020 - 2021): MHD circulator development and experimental characterization of liquid lithium films.

- [Electromagnetic pumps & MHD generators](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/em_99_other/) (UNIST, 2014 - 2021): Liquid metal circulation for reactors and accelerators, and magnetohydrodynamic power generation.

- [AI anomaly detection for the KOMAC linac](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/ot_01_komac_linac/) (KAERI, 2022 - 2023): An LSTM autoencoder for early detection of anomalies in quadrupole magnet operation.

- [Flow channel design for OLED manufacturing](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/tf_03_oled_display/) (KAERI, 2022): Reinforcement learning for temperature uniformity in display manufacturing susceptors.

- [Thermal and structural engineering at FRIB](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/tf_99_other/) (FRIB, 2024 - 2026): Thermal and structural analysis of beam intercepting devices, shielding, and target systems.

- [Static beam dump AI optimization](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/tf_01_frib_beam_dump/) (FRIB, 2023 - 2026): Global and local AI search with thermal model evaluation and 3D verification for static beam dump design.

- [Rotating beam dump development](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/tf_04_rotating_beam_dump/) (FRIB, 2024 - Present): Leading fabrication and installation across materials, systems engineering, thermomechanics, and radiation.

- [AI designed nuclear heat exchangers](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/tf_02_smr_heat_exchanger/) (KAERI, 2021 - 2023): Reinforcement learning for heat exchanger design, connected to metal 3D printing and experimental testing.

- [3D printable electromagnetic pump](https://geunhyeong.com/projects/em_01_3d_printable_emp/) (KAERI, 2023 - 2024): A single body DC pump concept designed for liquid metal circulation and metal 3D printing.

## Published articles (SCIE)

### Optimization of the FRIB Beam Dump: A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm and Reinforcement Learning Approach (2026)
- Authors: Geunhyeong Lee, J. Song, R. Quispe-Abad, M. Patil, T. Kanemura
- Journal: Nuclear Science and Techniques, 37, 184
- Keywords: genetic algorithm, reinforcement learning, FRIB, beam dump, optimization
- Key finding: Hybrid genetic algorithm and soft actor-critic (SAC) deep reinforcement learning redesign of the FRIB static beam dump for 20 kW to 50 kW operation, increasing simulated average power-handling capability by 72%.
- Citation: Lee, G., Song, J., Quispe-Abad, R., Patil, M., & Kanemura, T. (2026). Optimization of the FRIB Beam Dump: A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm and Reinforcement Learning Approach. Nuclear Science and Techniques, 37, 184. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41365-026-02020-2

### Conceptual Design of a 3D-Printable DC Electromagnetic Pump for Additive Manufacturing (2026)
- Authors: Geunhyeong Lee
- Journal: Nuclear Engineering and Technology, 58(1), 103916
- Keywords: electromagnetic pump, 3D printing, additive manufacturing, liquid metal
- Key finding: Solo-authored conceptual design of a 3D-printable DC electromagnetic pump using opposing permanent magnets, achieving 10.5 bar simulated developed pressure at 330 A (52% less input current than a helical pump).

### Deep learning-based anomaly detection in drift tube quadrupole operation for the KOMAC LINAC (2025)
- Authors: D.H. Kim, H.S. Kim, H.J. Kwon, Y. Yu, Geunhyeong Lee
- Journal: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology, 62(8), 709-714
- Keywords: deep learning, anomaly detection, LSTM, particle accelerator
- Key finding: LSTM autoencoder anomaly detection for KOMAC LINAC drift-tube quadrupole power supplies, detecting early anomaly signatures in five of ten historical voltage-fault cases, 30.7 to 286.6 minutes before the recorded voltage fault.
- Citation: Kim, D.H., Kim, H.S., Kwon, H.J., Yu, Y., & Lee, G. (2025). Deep learning-based anomaly detection in drift tube quadrupole operation for the KOMAC LINAC. Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology, 62(8), 709-714. https://doi.org/10.1080/00223131.2025.2464742

### Numerical investigation and comparison of the rectangular, cylindrical, and helical-type DC electromagnetic pumps (2017)
- Authors: Geunhyeong Lee, H.R. Kim
- Journal: Magnetohydrodynamics, 53(2), 429-438
- Keywords: electromagnetic pump comparison, rectangular EMP, cylindrical EMP, helical EMP
- Key finding: Comparative numerical analysis of rectangular, cylindrical, and helical DC electromagnetic pumps (6 cc/s, 10 bar at 300 C liquid lithium), showing the helical design requires 12% of the current of rectangular and cylindrical pumps.
- Citation: Lee, G., & Kim, H.R. (2017). Numerical investigation and comparison of the rectangular, cylindrical, and helical-type DC electromagnetic pumps. Magnetohydrodynamics, 53(2), 429-438. https://doi.org/10.22364/mhd.53.2.23
